correctness.rationale: For fixed n and m, the weighted interval Rayleigh quotient is asymptotically C_(n,m) a^(2n+1). A monic rescaled Legendre polynomial gives an upper bound; numerator O(a^(2n+1)) forces coefficient j to be O(a^(n-j)) by fixed-degree norm equivalence, and full-interval normalization then fixes the leading-coefficient magnitude. The unique monic Legendre minimizer identifies the matching lower bound and scaled polynomial shape. Spherical-harmonic azimuthal separation reduces each sector to weight (1-z^2)^m and degree n=L-m; nonzonal powers are smaller than 2L+1, so their eigenvalues are larger. Courant-Fischer gives a zonal second eigenvalue at least order a^(2L-1), yielding eventual simplicity and scaled Gauss-Legendre zeros. A high-precision checker verifies finite L<=5 examples, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The geometric equatorial Slepian operator, azimuthal separation, zonal numerical eigenfunctions and orthogonal polynomials are established prior work. Inspected primary 2006 belt Slepian work and 2020 application do not derive fixed-L thin-belt least-eigenvalue asymptotics with exact binomial constants, eventual zonal least eigenvector and scaled Gauss-Legendre nodal limit. value.rationale: The geometry is motivated by latitudinally limited spherical observations. The sharp all-bandwidth (fixed L) power a^(2L+1) and normalized binomial constant quantify the worst attainable continuum stability, and the asymptotic zonal optimizer and Gauss–Legendre nodes describe a nontrivial symmetry and nodal law. The joint quantitative spectral/nodal statement is not an arbitrary finite invariant, isolated experiment or routine numeric increment. The lack of a bandwidth-uniform estimate is explicitly limited.
